record.paper_title: High Open-Circuit Voltages in Lead-Halide Perovskite Solar Cells – Experiment, Theory and Open Questions
record.original_question: What experimental or analysis methods can separately quantify layer-specific contributions to series resistance in perovskite solar cells and measure how the internal quasi-Fermi level splitting in the perovskite absorber couples to the external quasi-Fermi level splitting at the contacts at the maximum power point?

evidence.quote: While it is generally easy to measure lumped series resistances in solar cells [97,98], it is more difficult to disentangle [99,100] the influence of different layers on the series resistance. Thus, methods are needed that measure how the internal quasi-Fermi level splitting in the perovskite absorber is coupled to the external quasi-Fermi level splitting at the contacts at the maximum power point.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multilayer thin-film solar cell consisting of a lead-halide perovskite absorber sandwiched between an electron-transport layer and a hole-transport layer, each in contact with a metal electrode. Under steady-state illumination at the maximum power point, define the following quantities:

1. The lumped series resistance R_s of the device, defined operationally from the current–voltage characteristic. Decompose R_s as R_s = Σ_i R_i, where each R_i is the contribution to the total series resistance arising from a single layer i (absorber, electron-transport layer, hole-transport layer, and the two electrode/interface contacts).

2. The internal quasi-Fermi level splitting Δμ_int(x) = E_{F,n}(x) − E_{F,p}(x) inside the perovskite absorber as a function of position x, where E_{F,n} and E_{F,p} are the electron and hole quasi-Fermi levels.

3. The external quasi-Fermi level splitting Δμ_ext = qV_ext at the metallic contacts at the maximum power point, where V_ext is the externally measured voltage.

Problem. Devise an experimental procedure (or combined experimental–analytical methodology) that:

(a) separately determines each layer-resolved resistance contribution R_i from in-operando measurements on a complete device, and

(b) quantitatively measures the coupling between the spatially averaged internal splitting ⟨Δμ_int⟩ in the absorber and the external splitting Δμ_ext at the maximum power point, i.e., determines the loss Δμ_loss = ⟨Δμ_int⟩ − Δμ_ext attributable to each transport/contact layer.

Prove or characterize, within a suitable drift-diffusion model of the device, that the proposed methodology uniquely recovers the set {R_i} and the splitting losses, and provide error bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns experimental/analytical methodology in perovskite photovoltaics. While techniques such as transmission-line impedance spectroscopy, photoluminescence quasi-Fermi-level imaging, and Suns-V_oc analyses have been developed and partially address layer-resolved resistance and internal-vs-external splitting comparisons, no single fully validated method that simultaneously and uniquely separates all layer contributions and rigorously couples internal to external Δμ at MPP is established in the literature. The problem remains broadly open as posed.

status_evidence.title: High Open-Circuit Voltages in Lead-Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
status_evidence.snippet: Methods are needed that measure how the internal quasi-Fermi level splitting in the perovskite absorber is coupled to the external quasi-Fermi level splitting at the contacts at the maximum power point.
status_evidence.claim: Identifies the layer-resolved series resistance and internal-vs-external QFLS coupling at MPP as an open methodological challenge.
